

# 3. Detailed Use Cases

## Overview

Requirements gathering activities identified a range of user groups that will contribute to, operate, or consume Ecosystem Indicator Workflows (EIWs). The use cases below represent the most common and highest-priority applications identified through workshops, user stories, and stakeholder consultations. These use cases informed the prioritisation of workflow functionality and the staged development roadmap. ## UC01 – Develop a New Ecosystem Indicator for a Target Ecosystem

| Attribute        | Description                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Ecologist / Conservation Scientist (UG01)                                                    |
| Supporting Users | Research Software Engineer (UG02), Data Scientist (UG03)                                     |
| Purpose          | Develop an ecosystem indicator for a previously unassessed ecosystem type.                   |
| Trigger          | A new ecosystem assessment, conservation program, or research project requires an indicator. |

### Workflow

1. Define the target ecosystem using the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology.
2. Define the intended assessment purpose (e.g. Red List assessment, Green Status assessment, ecosystem accounting).
3. Select ecosystem and indicator datasets.
4. Configure or adapt an existing workflow.
5. Run calculations and validation steps.
6. Review outputs and uncertainty estimates.
7. Publish results and workflow documentation.

### Outputs

* Indicator values
* Maps and visualisations
* Workflow documentation
* Validation and uncertainty reports

### Impact

Reduces the effort required to develop new indicators while increasing consistency, transparency, and reproducibility across ecosystem assessments. This use case emerged as a high-priority scenario during workshop discussions around workflow adaptability. ## UC02 – Adapt an Existing Workflow to a New Ecosystem

| Attribute        | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Ecologist / Technical Analyst (UG01, UG03)                                   |
| Supporting Users | RSE (UG02)                                                                   |
| Purpose          | Reuse an existing workflow for another ecosystem type or assessment purpose. |

### Workflow

1. Locate a suitable workflow in the workflow catalogue.
2. Identify ecosystem-specific components.
3. Replace ecosystem definitions, datasets and parameters.
4. Re-run workflow using the new ecosystem context.
5. Validate outputs.

### Outputs

* Adapted workflow
* Updated metadata and documentation
* New indicator outputs

### Impact

Reduces duplication of effort and accelerates ecosystem assessments. Workshop participants consistently identified workflow adaptability as one of the most important requirements for the EIW program. ## UC03 – Produce Indicators for State of the Environment Reporting

| Attribute        | Description                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Primary User     | Environmental Policy Analyst / Government Reporting Officer (UG06)                                     |
| Supporting Users | Ecologists, Analysts                                                                                   |
| Purpose          | Generate indicators for State of the Environment reporting and other statutory reporting requirements. |

### Workflow

1. Identify reporting requirements.
2. Select approved indicator workflows.
3. Access published outputs and provenance records.
4. Generate reporting products.
5. Incorporate outputs into reporting systems.

### Outputs

* Reporting tables
* Indicator summaries
* Maps
* Audit and provenance records

### Impact

Supports consistent environmental reporting and reduces the risk of non-comparable indicator methodologies between jurisdictions. Users identified reproducible and citable outputs as essential requirements. ## UC04 – Support Ecosystem Accounting and National Environmental Accounts

| Attribute        | Description                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Primary User     | Government Analyst (UG06)                                          |
| Supporting Users | Ecologist, Data Scientist                                          |
| Purpose          | Apply ecosystem indicators within ecosystem accounting frameworks. |

### Workflow

1. Identify accounting requirements.
2. Select indicators aligned with accounting frameworks.
3. Generate standardised outputs.
4. Integrate outputs into accounting systems and reporting products.

### Outputs

* Ecosystem condition accounts
* Indicator summaries
* Metadata and provenance documentation

### Impact

Improves consistency and transparency in ecosystem accounting processes while reducing manual preparation of indicator datasets. ## UC05 – Develop Indicators for Environmental Management

| Attribute        | Description                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Environmental Manager / Technical Practitioner (UG05)                                 |
| Supporting Users | Ecologists, Data Providers                                                            |
| Purpose          | Use ecosystem indicators to support management, restoration, and monitoring programs. |

### Workflow

1. Define management objectives.
2. Select appropriate ecosystem indicators.
3. Execute workflows using local data.
4. Monitor indicator trends over time.
5. Evaluate management outcomes.

### Outputs

* Indicator trend reports
* Dashboards
* Spatial products
* Monitoring summaries

### Impact

Enables evidence-based ecosystem management and supports long-term monitoring programs. Several workshop scenarios highlighted ongoing monitoring and indicator maintenance as a primary use of the workflows. ## UC06 – Integrate Heterogeneous Environmental Datasets

| Attribute        | Description                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Data Scientist / Technical Analyst (UG03)                                                                               |
| Supporting Users | Data Providers, Ecologists                                                                                              |
| Purpose          | Combine ecosystem distribution data, biological surveys, and remote sensing datasets into a single assessment workflow. |

### Workflow

1. Identify datasets.
2. Harmonise formats, classifications and metadata.
3. Align temporal and spatial scales.
4. Generate analysis-ready products.
5. Apply indicator calculations.

### Outputs

* Integrated datasets
* Harmonised workflows
* Indicator outputs

### Impact

Addresses one of the most common and time-consuming challenges identified by workshop participants: combining heterogeneous data sources into repeatable indicator workflows. ## UC07 – Publish and Maintain a Reproducible Workflow

| Attribute        | Description                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Research Software Engineer (UG02)                               |
| Supporting Users | Platform Administrator (UG09)                                   |
| Purpose          | Publish a workflow that can be reused and maintained over time. |

### Workflow

1. Package workflow components.
2. Define software dependencies.
3. Configure reproducible environments.
4. Register metadata and identifiers.
5. Publish workflow documentation.

### Outputs

* Workflow repository
* DOI and metadata records
* Documentation
* Containerised environment

### Impact

Supports long-term maintenance and reuse while ensuring workflows remain reproducible as software and data sources evolve. Reproducibility and software versioning were identified as critical concerns during workshops. ### Workflow

1. Search workflow catalogue.
2. Filter by ecosystem type, indicator type, or assessment framework.
3. Review documentation and examples.
4. Execute or adapt workflow.

### Outputs

* Adapted workflows

### Impact

Reduces duplication of effort and encourages workflow standardisation across organisations and jurisdictions. ## UC09 – Training and Skills Development

| Attribute        | Description                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Student / Early-Career Researcher (UG08)                         |
| Supporting Users | Ecologists, RSEs                                                 |
| Purpose          | Build capability in reproducible ecosystem assessment workflows. |

### Workflow

1. Attend workshops or training events.
2. Access worked examples.
3. Run demonstration workflows.
4. Modify workflows for new examples.
5. Contribute improvements.

### Outputs

* Trained users
* New contributors
* Community of practice

### Impact

Expands the user base and supports long-term sustainability of the workflow ecosystem. Training and documentation were identified as high-priority requirements across all workshop participants. ## UC10 – Support Nature-Related Reporting and Assurance

| Attribute        | Description                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary User     | Environmental Consultant / Assurance Practitioner (UG07)                                        |
| Supporting Users | Analysts, Ecologists                                                                            |
| Purpose          | Support environmental auditing, ecosystem accounting, and nature-related disclosure frameworks. |

### Workflow

1. Select workflows relevant to reporting requirements.
2. Generate standardised indicators.
3. Review audit and provenance records.
4. Produce client or organisational reporting products.

### Outputs

* Audit-ready indicators
* Reporting products
* Supporting evidence and provenance records

### Impact

Supports transparent, defensible and repeatable environmental assessments for government, industry and financial reporting applications. Consultation activities identified assurance and reporting applications as a growing area of demand. ### Summary

Across the requirements gathering process, ten recurring use cases were identified. These can be grouped into four broad categories:

1. **Workflow Development** (UC01, UC02, UC07)
2. **Assessment and Indicator Production** (UC03, UC04, UC05, UC06)
3. **Workflow Discovery and Reuse** (UC08)
4. **Capacity Building and Adoption** (UC09, UC10)

These use cases form the basis for prioritising functionality and defining the first and second tranches of workflow development activities described in subsequent sections.
